title: Meditations to begin (I.9–I.18)
hookLine: short meditations on creation, purpose, gifts, sin, death
tomorrow: an hour a day for prayer. who has that?

cards: College essays, job interviews, a first date: sooner or later someone asks a version of why are you here? The easy answer is a résumé.
Francis de Sales asks the same question and gives a bishop's first answer, in the meditations that open his book. Before you were born, he says, you weren't. You were simply nothing.
And God drew you out of that nothing, not because he needed you, but out of goodness.

teach.b: These meditations follow one shape. Begin by placing yourself in God's presence and asking for help. Then a few considerations, thoughts to turn over slowly.
Then affections and resolutions: what the heart feels, and what it decides. Then close with thanks.
The first is creation, the nothing from the hook. The second asks why.
God didn't put you in the world because he needed you, de Sales says, but to show his goodness in you.

teach.h: EVERY GIFT A TOOL FOR IT.
teach.b: So he gave you understanding to know him, memory to remember him, a will to love him, imagination to picture his kindness, eyes to see his works, a tongue to praise him.
Here's the line worth repeating: in that list, your gifts aren't rivals to the purpose. A good mind, a sharp eye, a strong voice are the tools for it.
Anything that pulls you away from that purpose, he says, is worth letting go.

From there the meditations move through gifts received, sin, death, judgment, hell and heaven, and end with a choice: of heaven, and of the devout life itself. Slow thoughts, one at a time, so the heart can decide.

how: Catholics practice meditation, or mental prayer, by reading a short passage, turning it over slowly in God's presence, and ending with a resolution and thanks, much as de Sales lays it out.

o: slow thoughts on why you were made, ending in thanks
breathing exercises to empty the mind of all thought
short prayers to memorize before starting school

games.q: the meditation's shape — tap the pairs.
p: what the heart feels and decides

s: Catholic meditation in de Sales means emptying your mind of all thought
it means turning a truth over slowly, then feeling, deciding and giving thanks.
de Sales says God made you because he needed you
not from need, he says, but to show his goodness in you.
his meditations end in a choice, including the devout life itself
the series closes with choosing heaven and the devout life.

games.q: your little brother asks at dinner, "why did God make me if he already had everyone else?" what could you say, from de Sales?
o: not because God needed you, but to show his goodness in you.
to fill a spot nobody else could, so God isn't lonely.
nobody knows; that's just a question to stop asking.
games.why: de Sales: God placed you in the world not from need, but to show his goodness in you, and gave you a mind, memory, will and eyes for it.

practice: Count de Sales's gifts on your fingers, slowly, one per breath: a mind to know, a memory to remember, a will to love, eyes to see, a voice to praise. At each one, notice the thing it did for you today.
If you pray, close with thanks, the way each of his meditations does.

wordCard.voice: Meditations to begin. De Sales's starting exercises: slow thoughts on creation, purpose, gifts, sin and death, each ending in a choice and thanks.

carryVoice: Keep this one: why made, not because God needed you, but because God is good. Until tomorrow.
